concept.name: TRIX
concept.definition: Jack Hutson's momentum oscillator (Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, early 1980s): the one-period percentage rate of change of a triple-smoothed exponential moving average (EMA of EMA of EMA), engineered to filter out price moves too small to matter.
concept.intuition: Three rounds of smoothing strip out noise; what remains turning up or down is, in theory, the significant trend cycle.
concept.mechanics: Compute EMA(n) of the close, then EMA(n) of that series, then EMA(n) again (default n = 15); TRIX = 100 x (tripleEMA_t - tripleEMA_{t-1}) / tripleEMA_{t-1}. Traded via signal-line (9-period EMA) crosses, zero-line crosses, and divergences.
concept.formula: EMA1 = EMA(C, n); EMA2 = EMA(EMA1, n); EMA3 = EMA(EMA2, n); TRIX = 100 x (EMA3_t - EMA3_{t-1}) / EMA3_{t-1}.
concept.failure_modes: The triple smoothing lags substantially - StockCharts' Intel example shows three of six signal-line crosses whipsawing in one stretch; in flat markets TRIX hugs zero with ambiguous crosses.
concept.misconceptions: Filtering out 'insignificant' moves also filters the early part of significant ones; TRIX's smoothness is bought with delay, not accuracy.
concept.example: If the triple-smoothed EMA rises from 100.0 to 100.2, TRIX prints +0.2 (percent) for that bar.
